5.5 recovery park public art scope change.
Thank you, Mr. Chair. This report is to inform committee that administration has adjusted the scope of the public art project plan for the new

waste diversion facility known as recovery park recovery park is a facility separated from the landfill where the public can deposit materials not intended for the landfill thus improving recycling options for residents.
The public art component to the project was identified as part of the overall scope of the project in the June 2021 report to EUCS on the overall budget for recovery park.
This plan public art is consistent with the intentions identified within the public art policy.

The public art is meant to enhance the design of the facility while at the same time serving as a communication or education tool regarding the importance of recycling and environmental sustainability.
With the scope change instead of a single artwork at recovery park, there will now be three artworks.
And we'll be located at recovery park itself while two others will be in different locations in the city.
These locations will be determined by administration and consultation with the successful artists and stakeholders.
Having three artworks at three locations will enhance the awareness of recovery park and broaden the city's efforts in communicating the importance of environmental sustainability.
There's no financial implication to this scope change. The RFQ remains at 275,000 plus 35,000 in contingency.
The funds are consultants, design, fabricate and install three works of arts.
And there are a number of administration available if there are any questions on this report.
